title: Recurrence relations, steps and branching
transcript: A recurrence tells you how a new state follows from earlier ones. Write the starting state and exactly what is repeated. If a state can be reached in more than one way, split the count by the final step. This can turn a branching tree into a short table.

AMC Upper Primary questions can use growing shapes or repeated moves. Translate the pattern into a stated rule before extending it. In a Mawa style investigation, change a starting rule or block one route. Explain how that adjustment spreads through the table.
Start a sequence at six. Add four to get each next term. What are the first four terms? Remember the starting value already counts as the first term.

The first addition produces ten. Repeat the same addition to get fourteen, then eighteen. Each difference is the same, so the rule predicts the list from its first term without any guess about the pattern.
A display starts at four. Each new reading is twice the last reading, minus one. Find its value after five changes. Try tracking the distance from one as well as the reading itself.

If a reading equals one plus a gap, doubling and subtracting one makes it one plus twice that gap. The gap doubles each time. The first gap is three. After five changes it is three times two to the power five. Add back the fixed one. The final reading is ninety-seven. Compare the first two steps to check the pattern.

Start on rung zero. A move goes up one or two rungs. Rung three is broken, so no route can land there. How many different move sequences finish exactly on rung nine? Count by the last jump onto each rung.

There is one way to be at the start: make no jumps. There are zero ways to land on the broken rung. To arrive at an allowed rung, the previous rung is either one below or two below. Add the counts of those disjoint kinds of route. Fill the table in order. The two entries just before the finish are six and ten. Their sum is sixteen.

The broken rung stops landings, but a jump of two can go over it. That is why an open rung after it can still have a positive count. The last-jump cases partition the routes. No route can end with both a one-rung jump and a two-rung jump.

Put one at the starting state when counting routes. The one empty route is what gives the first legal jump a route to extend. A broken rung removes the routes landing there. A move that jumps over it can still be legal.

State the starting values and the recurrence. Work in an order where every entry you need has already been found. Check the first steps and any exceptional states. If counting routes, explain why the last-step cases cannot overlap.
